topic: AI marketing doesn't need a team or budget
hook: Most people think AI marketing needs a team and a budget. Mine needed one file and a Tuesday afternoon.
caption:
Most people think AI marketing needs a team and a budget. Mine needed one file and a Tuesday afternoon.

I almost didn't bother. It sounded like a whole IT project. It's not. I wrote down what I sell, who buys it, and my one strong opinion, saved it as a single brief, and every AI tool I use now reads that first before it writes a word.

topic: 212 dead leads recovered with AI follow-up
hook: 212 dead leads. 19 replies in 48 hours. That's what AI follow-up did.
caption:
212 dead leads. 19 replies in 48 hours. That's what AI follow-up did.

A client handed me a list of 212 leads that had gone cold, some untouched for 6 months. I set up an AI follow-up sequence that texted each one a short, personal check-in based on what they'd originally asked about. In 48 hours, 19 people replied. 3 booked calls. 1 became a $4,200 client by Friday.

The leads didn't need a new offer. They needed someone to actually follow up.

Tag someone who's sitting on a dead leads list right now.

topic: Automation clients had no visibility into which leads converted
hook: 3 of my last 5 automation clients had the exact same blind spot.
caption:
3 of my last 5 automation clients had the exact same blind spot. AI follow-up was running perfectly. Nobody could tell you which leads it actually closed.

The bot was texting leads back and booking calls just fine. But nothing logged the outcome, so no one on the team knew which lead source was actually paying the bills. I added a notify-and-log step to a client's stack this week: every booked call fires a text to the owner and logs the source, response time, and result in one sheet. Now they know which channel pays, not just which one gets clicks.

Tag a business owner who has automation running with zero idea which leads it's actually converting.

topic: HVAC company recovers after-hours calls with AI voice agent (v1)
hook: 37 missed calls. 4 booked jobs. 0 dollars spent on more ads.
caption:
37 missed calls. 4 booked jobs. 0 dollars spent on more ads.

I set up an AI voice agent for an HVAC client last week. It answers every missed call in under 10 seconds, asks 3 qualifying questions, and books straight into the calendar if the job's a fit. In 7 days it caught 37 calls the front desk missed and turned 4 straight into booked jobs, most of them after hours.

topic: HVAC company recovers after-hours calls with AI voice agent
hook: An HVAC company was losing 1 in 3 after hours calls.
caption:
An HVAC company was losing 1 in 3 after hours calls. Nobody picked up, nobody called back, the job went to the competitor down the street.

I built them an AI voice agent that answers every call, asks the right diagnostic questions, and books straight into their calendar. First week live: 11 jobs booked overnight, average ticket $340. The owner never touched a script. It just needed to sound like someone who actually cared the AC was dead at 11pm.

topic: What Nate Herk's one-prompt company build reveals about small business execution gaps
hook: The prompt is not the interesting part. The 40 steps it skipped are.
caption:
The prompt is not the interesting part. The 40 steps it skipped are.

Nate Herk gave an AI a single prompt this week and it produced a landing page, launch videos, a business plan, and market research in one sitting. Impressive demo. But the part that matters for a real business isn't "AI can build a company." It's that every one of those 40 small steps between idea and shipped thing is exactly where most small businesses actually get stuck, not on ideas.

Most of my clients don't need a new company built. They need the 3 boring steps between "good idea" and "live and taking leads" handled without sitting on a to-do list for 6 weeks.

Tag a business owner who has 10 good ideas and 0 of them shipped.
